questions.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with chronic kidney disease (CKD) or told your kidney function (eGFR) is below normal?
questions.source: KDIGO CKD guidelines 2022; NKF staging criteria

questions.text: If you are on dialysis, what type and how often?
questions.source: KDIGO CKD 2022; USRDS annual data report

questions.text: How much plain water or unsweetened fluid do you typically drink per day?
questions.source: EFSA dietary reference values for water 2010; Borghi et al. NEJM 1996 (kidney stones)

questions.text: How would you describe your salt / sodium intake?

responses.label: Low — rarely add salt, avoid processed food
Moderate — some processed food, occasional salt
High — daily processed food, frequent salt addition
Very high — processed food most meals + extra salt

questions.source: He & MacGregor Lancet 2002; KDIGO CKD nutrition 2020

questions.text: How much protein do you typically eat per day? (include meat, fish, eggs, dairy, protein supplements)

responses.label: High (1.2–2 g/kg/day) — gym diet or frequent meat
Very high (>2 g/kg/day) — protein supplements daily

questions.source: Kalantar-Zadeh et al. JASN 2017; KDIGO CKD nutrition 2020

questions.text: Have you ever had a kidney stone (nephrolithiasis)?
questions.source: Stamatelou et al. Kidney Int 2003; Pearle et al. AUA guideline 2014

questions.text: How often do you eat high-oxalate foods: spinach, rhubarb, nuts, beetroot, chocolate, strong tea?
questions.source: Liebman & Al-Wahsh Adv Nutr 2011; EAU urolithiasis guideline 2023

questions.text: How often do you drink sugar-sweetened beverages, fruit juices, or energy drinks?
questions.source: Choi & Curhan NEJM 2008 (fructose-gout); Lustig et al. Nature 2012; Duffey & Popkin Am J Clin Nutr 2007

questions.text: How often do you use over-the-counter pain relievers (ibuprofen, naproxen, diclofenac, aspirin >1g/day)?
questions.source: Whelton et al. Ann Intern Med 1997; De Broe & Elseviers NEJM 1998

questions.text: Do you regularly take any herbal or dietary supplements? (e.g. kava, valerian, green tea extract, anabolic compounds, excessive vitamin A)

responses.label: Herbal: kava, valerian, comfrey, or weight-loss teas

questions.source: Navarro et al. Hepatology 2014; LiverTox database (NIH); Stickel et al. Gut 2011

questions.text: How many urinary tract infections (UTIs) have you had in the past 12 months?
questions.source: Foxman B. Am J Med 2002; Hooton TM NEJM 2012

questions.text: Do you currently have any of these symptoms: burning on urination, frequency, urgency, cloudy or foul-smelling urine?

responses.label: Flank pain or fever (possible kidney involvement)

questions.source: Hooton TM NEJM 2012; Gupta et al. Ann Intern Med 2001

questions.text: Have you been told you have high uric acid (hyperuricemia) or gout?

responses.label: Yes — high uric acid only (no gout attacks)
Yes — gout attacks (≥1 in past year)

triggers.if_response: Yes — gout attacks (≥1 in past year)

questions.source: Zhu et al. Arthritis Rheum 2011; Feig et al. NEJM 2008 (uric acid-CKD)

questions.text: How often do you eat high-purine foods: red meat, organ meats (liver/kidney), shellfish, anchovies, sardines?

in: Yes — high uric acid only (no gout attacks)
Yes — gout attacks (≥1 in past year)

questions.source: Choi et al. NEJM 2004; Dalbeth et al. Nat Rev Rheumatol 2019

questions.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with fatty liver, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), or MAFLD?
questions.source: Chalasani et al. Hepatology 2018 AASLD/AGA guideline; Younossi et al. Hepatology 2016

questions.text: Have you been told your liver enzymes (ALT, AST, GGT, or ALP) were elevated on a blood test?
questions.source: Kwo et al. Am J Gastroenterol 2017; Pratt & Kaplan NEJM 2000

questions.text: How much of your diet comes from ultra-processed foods (fast food, packaged snacks, ready meals, frozen pizza)?
questions.source: Rauber et al. BMJ 2019; Srour et al. BMJ 2019 (NOVA classification UPF)

questions.text: Do you consume products sweetened with high-fructose corn syrup, agave, or large amounts of fruit juice daily?

responses.label: Yes — a few times a week

questions.source: Lustig et al. Nature 2012; Lim et al. J Clin Invest 2010 (fructose de novo lipogenesis)

questions.text: Have you been diagnosed with gallstones (cholelithiasis) or had your gallbladder removed?
questions.source: Portincasa et al. Lancet 2006; Stinton & Shaffer Gastroenterol Clin 2012

questions.text: Have you had multiple pregnancies, used oral contraceptives, or undergone rapid weight loss (>1 kg/week)?

responses.label: Oral contraceptive pill — current or past use
Rapid weight loss in past year (crash diet / bariatric)

questions.source: Bates & Everhart Gastroenterol 2007; Portincasa et al. Lancet 2006

questions.text: Have you noticed any of these: yellowing of skin/eyes (jaundice), abdominal swelling, easy bruising, or spider veins on skin?
questions.source: Heidelbaugh & Bruderly Am Fam Physician 2006; Runyon NEJM 2004

questions.text: When you drink alcohol, do you tend to drink until intoxicated or binge (4+ drinks in one session for women, 5+ for men)?

responses.label: No — I usually stop after 1–2 drinks
Occasionally binge (once a month or less)

questions.source: O'Shea et al. Hepatology 2010; AUDIT-C Babor et al. WHO 2001

questions.text: Have you been diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, prediabetes, or hypertension (high blood pressure)?
questions.source: KDIGO DM-CKD guideline 2022; Brunt et al. Nat Rev Dis Primers 2015

questions.text: How many cups of coffee do you drink per day?
questions.source: Kennedy et al. Aliment Pharmacol Ther 2016; Freedman et al. Hepatology 2009 (coffee-cirrhosis meta-analysis)

questions.text: How much moderate-to-vigorous physical activity do you get per week?
questions.source: Vilar-Gomez et al. Gastroenterology 2015 (exercise NAFLD); Pechter et al. Nephrol Dial Transplant 2003

questions.text: How has your weight changed in the past 6 months?
questions.source: Kral et al. Gastroenterology 1993 (rapid loss gallstones); Promrat et al. Hepatology 2010

questions.text: Do you experience unexplained fatigue, dark-coloured urine, or noticeable puffiness / swelling in your legs or face?
questions.source: KDIGO CKD 2022 clinical presentation; Heidelbaugh & Bruderly AFP 2006

questions.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with or tested positive for viral hepatitis (hepatitis B or C)?
questions.source: WHO global hepatitis report 2017; Terrault et al. Hepatology 2018 (HBV)

questions.text: Have you been told you have metabolic syndrome, or do you have a waist circumference >94 cm (men) / >80 cm (women) plus two or more of: high triglycerides, low HDL, high blood pressure, high fasting glucose?
questions.source: Alberti et al. Circulation 2009 (IDF/AHA harmonised definition); Lonardo et al. Gut 2015 (MetS-NAFLD)

questions.text: Do you experience recurring pain or discomfort in the right upper abdomen or right shoulder tip?
questions.source: Portincasa et al. Lancet 2006; Trowbridge et al. JAMA 2003
